question: What is the difference between asyncio.gather, asyncio.wait, and asyncio.create_task?
title: asyncio.gather vs asyncio.wait vs create_task
direct_answer: gather() runs awaitables concurrently and returns results in order when all complete — raises on first exception by default. wait() gives more control: you pass a set of tasks and choose FIRST_COMPLETED or ALL_COMPLETED; it returns (done, pending) sets so you can process results as they arrive. create_task() schedules a coroutine immediately and returns a Task — it runs concurrently without being awaited immediately, enabling fire-and-forget patterns.
interviewer_intent: Tests practical async knowledge — knowing which tool to pick for a given concurrency pattern.

sections.title: Choosing the right async concurrency primitive
sections.content:
gather() is the most common: await asyncio.gather(coro1(), coro2()) runs both concurrently and returns [result1, result2] in the same order as input. If any coroutine raises, gather re-raises immediately (return_exceptions=True to collect all results/exceptions instead of failing fast).

wait() gives FIRST_COMPLETED semantics: await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED) returns when the first task finishes. You get (done, pending) sets. Use for: racing multiple sources, timeout patterns, progressive result processing. Note: you must pass Task objects, not coroutines — wrap coroutines with create_task() first.

create_task() schedules a coroutine immediately — it starts running without being awaited. The task runs in the 'background' while your current coroutine continues. Useful for: triggering side effects that shouldn't block the main flow (send audit log, update cache), parallel initialization.

Timeout pattern: asyncio.wait_for(coro, timeout=5.0) raises asyncio.TimeoutError if the coroutine doesn't complete in time. Use for all external calls.

sections.title: Pattern comparison
sections.content:
import asyncio

async def slow(n: float, val: str) -> str:
    await asyncio.sleep(n)
    return val

# gather — all results, order preserved
async def demo_gather():
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        slow(0.3, 'a'), slow(0.1, 'b'), slow(0.2, 'c')
    )
    print(results)  # ['a', 'b', 'c'] — input order, not completion order

# gather with error handling
async def demo_gather_errors():
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        slow(0.1, 'a'),
        asyncio.sleep(0) or (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError('oops')),
        return_exceptions=True   # collect exceptions as values
    )
    for r in results:
        if isinstance(r, Exception):
            print(f'Error: {r}')

# wait — FIRST_COMPLETED race
async def demo_wait():
    tasks = {asyncio.create_task(slow(n, v))
             for n, v in [(0.3, 'slow'), (0.1, 'fast')]}
    done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
    winner = done.pop().result()
    print(f'First: {winner}')   # 'fast'
    for task in pending:
        task.cancel()           # cancel the rest

# create_task — fire and schedule immediately
async def demo_create_task():
    task = asyncio.create_task(slow(0.1, 'background'))
    # task is running concurrently while we do other work
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)   # other work
    result = await task         # now wait for it

# wait_for — timeout
async def demo_timeout():
    try:
        result = await asyncio.wait_for(slow(5.0, 'too slow'), timeout=1.0)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        print('Timed out!')

sections.title: Primitive selection guide
rows: Fails fast (or collect all with return_exceptions)

sections.title: Async primitive rules
items: gather(): most common pattern — concurrent run, ordered results
return_exceptions=True: collect errors instead of failing fast on first exception
wait() with FIRST_COMPLETED: race pattern, cancel pending tasks afterwards
create_task(): starts immediately without blocking — background work
Always timeout external calls: asyncio.wait_for(call(), timeout=5.0)

seo.metaTitle: asyncio.gather vs asyncio.wait vs create_task — Python Async Guide
seo.metaDescription: Python asyncio: gather for ordered concurrent results, wait for FIRST_COMPLETED racing, create_task for background work, wait_for for timeouts.

speakable_v2.hook: gather, wait, and create_task all run coroutines concurrently — but they answer different questions about when and how you want the results.

beats.content: gather is the default: run everything, wait for all, return results in input order. If one fails, the whole gather fails — unless you pass return_exceptions=True to collect exceptions as values.
wait gives you FIRST_COMPLETED semantics. You get (done, pending) sets — process the winner, cancel the rest. Use this for racing multiple data sources or implementing timeout-with-fallback patterns.

create_task schedules a coroutine immediately and returns a Task — it runs while you continue. Await the Task when you actually need the result. Useful for firing off audit logs or cache updates that shouldn't block the response.

speakable_v2.cap: Always wrap external calls with asyncio.wait_for. A hung external call with no timeout will hang your coroutine indefinitely.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Good follow-up: asyncio.Semaphore for rate-limiting concurrent tasks, or task cancellation patterns.
